$comment: Cases both editors must judge alike. Each case is a source and the issues expected for it, sorted by start, end and code; offsets count UTF-16 code units. An issue without start and end is checked by code only: the two JavaScript parsers do not always place a syntax error on the same character. fixes holds the whole source after each quick fix, in the order offered. The severity and message, where a case gives them, are checked as well. A case may give prefix, the attribute prefix of an aliased bundle, which is data- otherwise.

issues.message: A signal name holds no hyphen: Datastar's client reads one as a capital in an attribute key and as a hyphen in an expression or a patch, so Streamlord refuses "fooBar-baz" at runtime. Write fooBarBaz.

No key gives fooBar-baz back: the browser lowercases attribute names, and with __case.camel or __case.pascal Datastar turns every hyphen before a lower-case letter into a capital and reads fooBarBaz. Write it in one case.

div {
  dataSignals("fooBar", "1")
  dataOn("widgetLoaded", "x()") { once = true }
  dataClass("isOpen", "$" + "open")
  dataStyle("backgroundColor", "'red'")

  dataSignals("{fooBar: 1}")

  dataOnClick("@post('/Add')", { once = true })
  dataOnFetch("evt.detail.type === 'Started'") { window = true }
  dataRef("myRef")

  dataPersist("myKey")
  dataMatchMedia("isMobile", mediaQuery = "(max-width: 600px)")
}

issues.message: Written on the wire as data-signals:foo-bar, which Datastar reads back as the signal $fooBar: the browser lowercases attribute names, so a key is kebab-case. In HTML or a template you write it that way yourself.

Written on the wire as data-on:widget-loaded__case.camel, which Datastar reads back as the event widgetLoaded: the browser lowercases attribute names, so a key is kebab-case. In HTML or a template you write it that way yourself.

Written on the wire as data-class:is-open__case.camel, which Datastar reads back as the class isOpen: the browser lowercases attribute names, so a key is kebab-case. In HTML or a template you write it that way yourself.

Written on the wire as data-style:background-color, which Datastar reads back as the property background-color: the browser lowercases attribute names, so a key is kebab-case. In HTML or a template you write it that way yourself. A CSS property is written in kebab-case: data-style:background-color.

Written on the wire as data-signals:my-signal__case.pascal, which Datastar reads back as the signal $MySignal: the browser lowercases attribute names, so a key is kebab-case. In HTML or a template you write it that way yourself.

Written on the wire as data-on:custom-event__case.kebab, which Datastar reads back as a kebab-cased name: the browser lowercases attribute names, so a key is kebab-case. In HTML or a template you write it that way yourself.

Written on the wire as data-persist:my-key, which Datastar reads back as the attribute my-key: the browser lowercases attribute names, so a key is kebab-case. In HTML or a template you write it that way yourself.

Written on the wire as data-match-media:is-mobile, which Datastar reads back as the signal $isMobile: the browser lowercases attribute names, so a key is kebab-case. In HTML or a template you write it that way yourself.
